environment — not SPX.

## Consumer Defensive (XLP) — 2026-08-27

Object is the **near-session XLP environment**, not SPX and not a stock pick. Channel 1 numbers are used as given.

### Channel 1 tape (confirmation only)
XLP is a **chronic laggard**: **1d -0.29% vs SPY +0.02% (rel -0.31%)**, 3d rel **+0.28%**, 1w rel **+0.08%**, 1m rel **-4.31%**. The 1m relative is deeply negative — XLP has underperformed SPY by over 4% over the past month. Yesterday (08-26) XLP was the **worst-performing sector** (per etfaction). The 1d relative is a clear fade after the prior defensive run.

Macro panel as it maps here: **ES +0.31% / NQ +0.55%** (risk-on futures), Asia +0.1%, Europe +0.13%, VIX 15.21 (low), Fear & Greed 56.8 (Greed), real yields DFII10 2.32 (**-0.06 1d, -0.09 1w, -0.12 1m** — easing), 10Y 4.64 (-0.06 1d), **oil CL -1.11% / BZ -2.11%** (down), gold +1.45%, DXY -0.03% 1d. 5-day 10Y-SPX corr -0.292.

### Channel 2 — required categories

**1. Shared macro → this sector.** The dominant scheduled catalyst — **July core PCE — printed this morning: slightly hot** (headline 3.7% vs 3.6% expected, core 3.3% as expected). This is a **mild hawkish surprise** that pressured stocks lower early (per sedaily "Wall Street Slips as July PCE Inflation Tops Forecasts"), but indexes were "little changed" (Investopedia) and futures are now **risk-on** (ES +0.31%, NQ +0.55%). September rate-hike odds fell to 38% (Schwab). Treasury yields moved slightly higher on the headline miss. For a bond-proxy defensive, the slightly-hot PCE is a **mild duration headwind**, but real yields are **easing** this morning (DFII10 -0.06 1d, -0.12 1m) and oil is down hard (input relief). The risk-on futures (NQ +0.55% > ES +0.31%) are a **mild rotation away from defensives**. Net: neutral-to-slightly-negative for XLP. Do not force S0 negative merely because PCE exists (08-12 rule) — the print is out and largely digested. Same shock counted once: PCE + easing real yields + oil down = one rate/input regime, not three positives.

**2. Spine.**
- **Flight-to-safety RS vs cyclicals (primary):** MISS/weak. XLP 1d rel **-0.31%**, 1m rel **-4.31%**. The prior defensive leadership has faded; XLP is now a chronic laggard. Do not re-score the prior run as a fresh S1 positive (08-14 outsized-reversal rule).
- **Risk-on rotation away from defensives:** **HIT this morning.** NQ +0.55% vs ES +0.31%; risk-on futures. XLP was the worst sector yesterday.
- **Pricing power without volume collapse:** PARTIAL / carried. KO/PG quality bid was real last week; no fresh same-day beat. WMT's slowest US comps in six years is **stale (08-20)** and already absorbed.
- **Volume decline accelerating:** PARTIAL / carried. July retail sales -0.6% and WMT comps are known; not a same-morning print. Do not restack as a one-way FTS tailwind (08-17).

**3. Secondary.**
- **Input-cost relief (ag, packaging, freight):** PARTIAL HIT. Crude crash (CL -1.11%, BZ -2.11%) is freight/energy relief. Offset: wheat/corn still firm YoY, containerboard/packaging still hiking. Do not full-count oil-down twice (already the rate/input sign in S0).
- **Volume stabilization:** checked, nothing material and new — still the soft-volume regime.
- **Staples earnings / stable margins:** no fresh same-day XLP-weight beat. WMT is prior-week, not a new S1 negative (08-21).
- **Private-label vs brands:** HIT (structural). Circana/PLMA H1'26: store-brand units ~24%, +0.2% vs national brands -0.5%.
- **Rotation into/out of defensives:** **out** is the live premarket tell (risk-on futures, XLP worst sector yesterday).

**4. Breadth / leadership.** XLP was the **worst-performing sector** on 08-26 (per etfaction). The 1d relative is negative. This is not an ETF-up/names-flat failure; it's a broad sector fade. Single-ticker rule: WMT (~9.7%) is context; COST/PG/KO are the book. No high-beta chase.

**5. Flows / positioning.** Latest hard print: LSEG/Reuters, week through 08-19, **consumer-staples funds -$623M** inside -$3.1B sectoral outflows. XLP was not a standout create/redeem. 1m rel -4.31% is a chronic laggard, not a crowded-long extreme. S3 cannot confirm a bid and does not justify a washout bounce either.

**6. Catalysts / calendar.** **Core PCE printed this morning (slightly hot)** — the dominant catalyst is now out and largely digested. **Nvidia earnings due after the close today** — a binary event that could flip the tape risk-on or risk-off into tomorrow. Warsh Jackson Hole speech Fri 08-28. No further 8:30 ET high-impact print today. Do not one-way score the pending Nvidia/Fed week.

### Lesson / self-audit
- 08-21: WMT drop is **not** a fresh S1 negative; already absorbed.
- 08-18: risk-off + FTS counted **once**; notable needs live top-holding confirmation. No such confirmation today — XLP was worst sector yesterday.
- 08-17 retail-earnings-week trap is **off** — WMT has reported.
- 08-14 / 08-10: no fresh 8:30 catalyst beyond the now-out PCE, futures not ≥0.5%, mag hit-rate 0.4 → **do not stack into notable**. Multiplier ≤1.0.
- 08-11 oil-shock down/mild: **not triggered** (oil is down, not a Hormuz squeeze).
- 08-25/08-26 reversal tell: XLP led hard then gave back; the 1d rel is now negative. This supports a flat-to-down read.
- Same-shock: PCE + easing real yields + oil down = one rate/input regime, not three positives.
- Single-ticker: WMT is context, not the ETF call.
- Divergence: leading factors (risk-on rotation, chronic laggard) and S4 tape (negative 1d) **agree** — both defensive-negative. No leading-vs-tape fight.

**Read:** mild **relative down / contained absolute**. Risk-on futures + chronic 1m laggard + slightly-hot PCE point to XLP lagging SPY today. Offsets (easing real yields, oil down, gold up) cap the magnitude at flat-to-mild.

**0. FACTS**

XLP **−1.38%** vs SPY **+0.66%**, relative **−2.03%**. Open **85.31** → close **85.08**. Prior close was ~**86.27**, so the session **gapped down ~1.1%** and then faded another ~0.27% into the close (near the low). Direction **down**. Magnitude **notable** on both absolute and relative (not mild). Path: overnight/gap did most of the damage; cash session was a contained grind lower, not a crash.

---

**1. What drove the sector**

Primary: **risk-on rotation / equity-beta expansion into Nvidia/AI/tech**, which is the inverse of XLP’s flight-to-safety spine. NVDA printed **after the close on 08-26** (not after 08-27 close): revenue **$96.2B (+106% YoY)**, data center **$89.0B**, Q3 guide **$108B ±2%**. Cash session: NVDA **+8.74%** to **$227.98**; S&P **+0.72%** to **7,731**; Nasdaq **+1.57%**. Tech was the leader (~**+3.0% to +3.4%**); staples the laggard (~**−1.3% to −1.5%**).

Secondary, same-sign stack (not a second independent thesis):
- **Oil rebound** after the morning’s CL/BZ dump. DJ Newswires tied consumer-company weakness to **oil futures rebound + Treasury yields** and inflation/mortgage-rate worries. Morning had treated oil-down as **input relief**.
- **Volume/consumer-pressure confirmation** from **Hormel (HRL)** same-day: organic sales **−2%**, retail volume **−9%**, FY sales guide cut to **$12.1–$12.2B** from **$12.2–$12.5B**. HRL is **~0.43% of XLP** — outlier/sentiment, not the ETF math.
- Top book was **broad**, not a single-ticker: WMT/COST/PG/KO all ~**−1% to −2%**.

Yields were **not** the main shock: 10Y **~4.672%**, **little changed** into Jackson Hole. Duration was a mild overlay, not the driver.

---

**2. Morning S0–S4 vs reality (use morning numbers, no rewrite)**

Morning pipeline: S0 **0**, S1 **−1**, S2 **−1**, S3 **0**, S4 **−1**, mult **0.9**, total **−4.95**, **down / mild**, confidence **0.55**, mixed, divergence **False**.

| **S0 shared macro** | **0**. PCE “slightly hot but digested”; real yields easing; oil down = one rate/input regime; **do not one-way score pending Nvidia**. | NVDA was **already out AH 08-26**. Open tape was a **confirmed** tech-led risk-on session, not a binary pending event. S0 was too neutral. | **Undershot**. Direction of “not a FTS day” was right; intensity was wrong. |
| **S1 sector factors** | **−1**. Risk-on rotation HIT; FTS MISS; oil relief HIT (partial); WMT stale. | Rotation HIT, and harder. Oil **flipped** from relief to rebound headwind. HRL was a same-day volume tell, not a WMT re-litigation. | **Direction HIT, magnitude undershot**. |
| **S2 breadth** | **−1**. Worst sector 08-26, broad fade, not ETF-up/names-flat. | Confirmed: staples **worst or near-worst**; WMT/COST/PG/KO all red. | **HIT**. |
| **S3 flows** | **0**. Staples funds **−$623M** week through 08-19; not a washout bounce. | No evidence of a create/redeem bid. Chronic 1m laggard continued. | **HIT (neutral was fine)**. |
| **S4 tape** | **−1**. 1d rel **−0.31%**, 1m rel **−4.31%**. | Gap-down continuation, close near lows, rel **−2.03%**. | **HIT, then some**. |

**Direction HIT. Magnitude MISS** (called **mild**, printed **notable**). The write-up even tried to cap at **flat-to-mild**; the pipeline’s **mild** was still too small once NVDA was a live, already-printed risk-on shock.

---

**3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open**

- **Same shock, counted once:** NVDA beat + NQ>ES + XLP lag = **one** risk-on / anti-FTS factor. Do **not** add a separate “tech up” S0 and “rotation out of defensives” S1 as two full hits. Morning actually **undercounted** this shock by parking NVDA in “pending, do not score.”
- **Oil is a sign flip, not a second thesis:** morning CL **−1.11% / BZ −2.11%** was input relief (partial S1+). Session oil **rebounded ~+1.6%** and was cited as a consumer headwind. That is a **path change after the snapshot**, not a new independent driver.
- **HRL ≠ XLP:** ~**0.4%** weight. Useful as a **volume-decline** confirmation, illegal as the ETF call. Book names did the damage.
- **PCE vs NVDA:** slightly-hot PCE was **yesterday’s** print and largely in the morning tape. **Do not** restack PCE as today’s driver. Today’s incremental macro was **NVDA + oil bounce**.
- **Knowable at open: partially.**
  - **Yes:** risk-on futures (ES **+0.31%**, NQ **+0.55%**), XLP chronic 1m lag, 08-26 worst-sector fade, PCE already out.
  - **Yes, and morning missed it:** NVDA results/guide were **public the night before**. Treating them as “after the close **today**” was a **calendar error** that capped magnitude.
  - **No:** oil rebound during the session; HRL sales-cut print; exact size of the NVDA cash-session squeeze (**+8.7%**, Nasdaq **+1.6%**).

---

**4. Outliers inside the sector**

- **HRL:** sales miss, retail volume **−9%**, FY sales guide cut; shares reported **~−9%**. Too small to move XLP 1.4% alone; it is the **loudest volume-soft print**, not the spine.
- **DLTR:** same-day consumer/fuel commentary; not an XLP heavy. Ignore for ETF math.
- **WMT/COST/PG/KO:** the actual book, all down ~1–2%. This was a **sector fade**, not a meat-packer accident.
- No quality-bid exception (no KO/PG outperformance vs the ETF).
